assessment: Neurons develop and maintain rich electrophysiological properties that enable nervous systems to function. The question of how different neural properties are regulated by internal ion channel expression mechanisms remains unresolved. In this paper, Yang and colleagues address the question from an abstract perspective by asking how multiple constraints on the physiological properties of neurons, such as firing rate curves and energy efficiency, narrow down the available regulatory possibilities. Their results from a mixture of modelling and dynamic clamp experiments point to the existence of multiple parallel internal feedback loops for controlling ion channel expression in neurons, and derive conditions under which co-regulation mechanisms will fail.
